definitions.zh: a. 散光的, 矫正散光的
[计] 象散

examples.en: He wears glasses because he is astigmatic.
examples.zh: 他因为散光而戴眼镜。

examples.en: An astigmatic eye sees blurry images.
examples.zh: 散光的眼睛看到模糊的图像。

definitions.en: n. any creative group active in the innovation and application of new concepts and techniques in a given field (especially in the arts)
definitions.zh: n. 先锋派；前卫派

examples.en: The artist is part of the avant-garde movement.
examples.zh: 这位艺术家是先锋派运动的一员。

examples.en: Avant-garde music challenges traditional forms.
examples.zh: 前卫音乐挑战传统形式。

definitions.en: s inspiring awe or admiration or wonder
definitions.zh: a. 使人畏惧的

examples.en: The mountain view is truly awe-inspiring.
examples.zh: 山景确实令人敬畏。

examples.en: Her performance was awe-inspiring to everyone.
examples.zh: 她的表演让所有人感到敬畏。

definitions.en: n. A check; a relapse; a discouragement; a setback.
definitions.zh: n. 挫折, 倒退, 逆流, 涡流

examples.en: The project suffered a backset due to rain.
examples.zh: 项目因下雨而遭受挫折。

examples.en: This backset discouraged the team greatly.
examples.zh: 这次倒退极大地打击了团队。

definitions.en: v. decorate tastelessly
definitions.zh: vt. 俗丽地打扮(或装饰)

examples.en: She bedizens herself with cheap jewelry.
examples.zh: 她用廉价珠宝俗丽地打扮自己。

examples.en: They bedizen the room with too many decorations.
examples.zh: 他们用太多装饰品俗丽地装饰房间。

definitions.en: v. to work at or to absurd length
definitions.zh: vt. 痛打

definitions.en: v. attack verbally with harsh criticism
definitions.zh: [法] 殴打, 鞭打, 辱骂

examples.en: He belabors the point in his speech.
examples.zh: 他在演讲中反复强调这一点。

examples.en: Don't belabor the obvious; move on.
examples.zh: 不要痛打显而易见的事；继续吧。

definitions.en: v annoy persistently
definitions.zh: vt. 围, 围攻

examples.en: The army beleaguers the enemy fortress.
examples.zh: 军队围攻敌人的堡垒。

examples.en: Problems beleaguer the new company daily.
examples.zh: 问题每天困扰着这家新公司。

definitions.en: n. someone who assumes leadership of a movement or activity
definitions.zh: n. 系铃带头羊, 前导, 领导者

examples.en: This company is a bellwether in technology.
examples.zh: 这家公司是技术领域的领导者。

examples.en: The bellwether stock indicates market trends.
examples.zh: 领头羊股票指示市场趋势。

definitions.en: n. a spoken blessing
definitions.zh: n. 祝福

examples.en: The priest gave a benison to the crowd.
examples.zh: 牧师向人群赐予祝福。

examples.en: We received a benison from the elder.
examples.zh: 我们收到了长者的祝福。

definitions.en: s. given to or marked by the consumption of alcohol
definitions.zh: a. 饮酒的, 嗜酒的, 吸水的
[医] 吸水的

examples.en: He is known as a bibulous person at parties.
examples.zh: 他在聚会上以嗜酒闻名。

examples.en: The bibulous sponge absorbs water quickly.
examples.zh: 吸水的海绵快速吸收水分。

definitions.en: n people who have severe visual impairments, considered as a group
definitions.zh: n. 百叶窗；盲人（常用复数）

examples.en: The blinds help the visually impaired people.
examples.zh: 盲人辅助设施帮助视觉障碍者。

examples.en: We close the blinds to block sunlight.
examples.zh: 我们关上百叶窗以阻挡阳光。

definitions.en: n a feeling of evil to come
definitions.zh: a. 凶兆的, 预兆的

definitions.en: v indicate by signs
definitions.zh: n. 凶兆, 前兆, 预感

examples.en: The dark clouds are boding a storm.
examples.zh: 乌云预示着暴风雨。

examples.en: She felt a boding of evil to come.
examples.zh: 她感到一种凶兆即将来临。

definitions.en: s. unproductive of success
definitions.zh: a. 无用的, 无益的
[法] 无益的, 无用的

examples.en: His efforts were bootless and wasted.
examples.zh: 他的努力是无用的且浪费了。

examples.en: The bootless attempt ended in failure.
examples.zh: 无益的尝试以失败告终。

definitions.en: v. edit by omitting or modifying parts considered indelicate
definitions.zh: vt. 删除, 删改

examples.en: The editor bowdlerizes the book for children.
examples.zh: 编辑为儿童删改这本书。

examples.en: They bowdlerize the movie to remove violence.
examples.zh: 他们删改电影以去除暴力内容。

definitions.en: s (used of an ill-mannered child) impolitely unruly
definitions.zh: a. 被惯坏的；讨厌的；无礼的, 幼稚的

examples.en: The brattish child threw a tantrum in the store.
examples.zh: 那个被惯坏的孩子在商店里发脾气。

examples.en: His brattish behavior annoyed everyone nearby.
examples.zh: 他无礼的行为惹恼了附近所有人。

definitions.en: n an instrument for measuring the distance between two points (often used in the plural)
definitions.zh: pl. 测径规, 卡钳

definitions.en: v measure the diameter of something with calipers
definitions.zh: [化] 卡钳

examples.en: The mechanic uses calipers to measure the part.
examples.zh: 机械师用卡钳测量零件。

examples.en: Calipers are essential for precise measurements.
examples.zh: 测径规对于精确测量是必需的。

definitions.en: v charge falsely or with malicious intent; attack the good name and reputation of someone
definitions.zh: vt. 中伤, 诽谤
[法] 诬蔑, 诽谤, 中伤

examples.en: He tries to calumniate his rival with lies.
examples.zh: 他试图用谎言诽谤他的对手。

examples.en: Do not calumniate others without evidence.
examples.zh: 不要在没有证据的情况下中伤他人。

definitions.en: s. tending to find and call attention to faults
definitions.zh: a. 吹毛求疵的, 挑剔的

examples.en: Her captious remarks often start arguments.
examples.zh: 她吹毛求疵的评论经常引发争论。

examples.en: A captious critic finds fault with everything.
examples.zh: 挑剔的批评者对每件事都吹毛求疵。

definitions.en: n. a rate that is rapid
definitions.zh: n. 迅速, 快速

examples.en: The cheetah moves with great celerity.
examples.zh: 猎豹以极快的速度移动。

examples.en: He completed the task with surprising celerity.
examples.zh: 他以惊人的迅速完成了任务。

definitions.en: a. of or relating to the head
definitions.zh: a. 头的
[医] 头的, 头侧的

examples.en: The cephalic region includes the head.
examples.zh: 头部区域包括头。

examples.en: Cephalic injuries require immediate attention.
examples.zh: 头部受伤需要立即关注。

definitions.en: n a crude uncouth ill-bred person lacking culture or refinement
definitions.zh: n. 下层自由民, 中世纪的农民, 出身低贱的人, 乡下人, 粗暴的人, 吝啬鬼, 守财奴

examples.en: The churl refused to share his food.
examples.zh: 那个吝啬鬼拒绝分享他的食物。

examples.en: Don't be a churl; be generous to others.
examples.zh: 不要做粗暴的人；对他人慷慨些。

definitions.en: s roundabout and unnecessarily wordy; (`ambagious' is archaic)
definitions.zh: a. 拐弯抹角的, 迂回的

examples.en: His circumlocutory speech confused the audience.
examples.zh: 他拐弯抹角的演讲让观众困惑。

examples.en: Avoid circumlocutory language in your writing.
examples.zh: 在写作中避免迂回的语言。

definitions.en: s not ready to receive to new ideas
definitions.zh: a. 思想保守的, 不易接受新鲜事物的, 有成见的

examples.en: A closed-minded person rejects new ideas easily.
examples.zh: 思想保守的人容易拒绝新想法。

examples.en: Being closed-minded limits your growth.
examples.zh: 思想保守限制你的成长。

definitions.en: v. cause surfeit through excess though initially pleasing
definitions.zh: vt. 使吃饱, 使过饱, 使厌腻
vi. 倒胃口

examples.en: Too much sweet food can cloy your taste.
examples.zh: 太多甜食会让你倒胃口。

examples.en: The rich dessert began to cloy after a while.
examples.zh: 过了一会儿，油腻的甜点开始让人厌腻。

definitions.en: n a familiar name for a person (often a shortened version of a person's given name)
definitions.zh: n. 姓, 名字, 绰号

definitions.en: n the name used to identify the members of a family (as distinguished from each member's given name)
definitions.zh: [法] 姓, 名字, 别名

examples.en: His cognomen is 'Slim' because he is tall.
examples.zh: 他的绰号是“瘦子”，因为他很高。

examples.en: The family cognomen is Smith.
examples.zh: 这个家族的姓是史密斯。

definitions.en: a. having cold blood (in animals whose body temperature is not internally regulated)
definitions.zh: a. 冷血的, (贬)无情的, 残酷的
[医] 冷血的

examples.en: Snakes are cold-blooded animals.
examples.zh: 蛇是冷血动物。

examples.en: The cold-blooded murder shocked the town.
examples.zh: 这起残酷的谋杀震惊了小镇。

definitions.en: n. any substance that can be used as food
definitions.zh: a. 可吃的
n. 食物

examples.en: The store sells various comestible items.
examples.zh: 这家商店出售各种可吃的物品。

examples.en: Pack some comestibles for the trip.
examples.zh: 为旅行打包一些食物。

definitions.en: n. a disposition or tendency to yield to the will of others
definitions.zh: n. 谦恭, 殷勤, 顺从

examples.en: Her complaisance makes her easy to work with.
examples.zh: 她的谦恭使她容易共事。

examples.en: He showed complaisance by agreeing to help.
examples.zh: 他通过同意帮忙表现出顺从。

definitions.en: v. combine two strings to form a single one
definitions.zh: vt. 如锁链般连接, 使连锁, 连结

definitions.en: v. add by linking or joining so as to form a chain or series
definitions.zh: a. 连锁的, 连结的

examples.en: You can concatenate two strings in programming.
examples.zh: 你可以在编程中连接两个字符串。

examples.en: The events concatenate to form a story.
examples.zh: 这些事件连接起来形成一个故事。

definitions.en: s. fitting or appropriate and deserved; used especially of punishment
definitions.zh: a. (尤指惩罚)应得的, 适宜的

examples.en: The criminal received a condign punishment.
examples.zh: 罪犯得到了应得的惩罚。

examples.en: Condign reward followed his hard work.
examples.zh: 他努力工作后得到了适宜的奖励。

definitions.en: v. express one's sympathetic grief, on the occasion of someone's death
definitions.zh: vi. 哀悼, 慰问, 吊唁

examples.en: I condole with you on your loss.
examples.zh: 我对你的损失表示哀悼。

examples.en: They came to condole with the family.
examples.zh: 他们来向这家人吊唁。

definitions.en: v become or cause to become obstructed
definitions.zh: vt. 使充满, 使拥塞, 使充血
vi. 充塞, 充血, 拥挤

examples.en: Traffic will congest the city center.
examples.zh: 交通会使市中心拥堵。

examples.en: The cold made his nose congest.
examples.zh: 感冒让他的鼻子充血。

definitions.en: n. an overall summary
definitions.zh: n. 概观, 一览表, 大纲

examples.en: The conspectus gives an overview of the book.
examples.zh: 概观给出了这本书的概述。

examples.en: Read the conspectus before the meeting.
examples.zh: 在会议前阅读大纲。

definitions.en: v become tight or as if tight
definitions.zh: vt. 压缩, 使收缩, 使收敛

examples.en: The cold air made his skin constringe.
examples.zh: 冷空气使他的皮肤收缩。

examples.en: The medicine will constringe the blood vessels.
examples.zh: 这种药会收缩血管。

definitions.en: s. wilfully obstinate; stubbornly disobedient
definitions.zh: a. 不听命令的, 反抗权威的, 反抗法院命令的
[法] 反抗法院命令的, 不听命令的

examples.en: The contumacious student refused to obey the teacher.
examples.zh: 这个反抗的学生拒绝服从老师。

examples.en: Her contumacious behavior got her into trouble.
examples.zh: 她反抗的行为给她带来了麻烦。

definitions.en: n. willful refusal to appear before a court or comply with a court order; can result in a finding of contempt of court
definitions.zh: n. 拒不服从, 反抗权威

definitions.en: n. obstinate rebelliousness and insubordination; resistance to authority
definitions.zh: [法] 不听法院命令, 藐视法庭

examples.en: His contumacy led to a court fine.
examples.zh: 他的拒不服从导致了法庭罚款。

examples.en: Contumacy is not tolerated in this school.
examples.zh: 这所学校不容忍反抗权威。

definitions.en: n a rude expression intended to offend or hurt
definitions.zh: n. 无礼, 傲慢, 侮辱

examples.en: She faced contumely from her rude coworkers.
examples.zh: 她面对粗鲁同事的侮辱。

examples.en: Contumely can hurt a person's feelings deeply.
examples.zh: 侮辱会深深伤害一个人的感情。

definitions.en: v. fold into ridges
definitions.zh: vt. 使起皱, 成波状
vi. 起皱
a. 有皱的, 起皱的, 波状的

examples.en: The machine can corrugate the cardboard easily.
examples.zh: 这台机器能轻松使纸板起皱。

examples.en: Rain caused the paper to corrugate slightly.
examples.zh: 雨水使纸张稍微起皱。

definitions.en: v. act with artful deceit
definitions.zh: v. 欺骗, 瞒

examples.en: He tried to cozen the old man out of money.
examples.zh: 他试图欺骗老人的钱。

examples.en: Don't let anyone cozen you with false promises.
examples.zh: 不要让任何人用虚假承诺欺骗你。

definitions.en: v hold back
definitions.zh: vt. 妨害, 阻碍, 使受苦
n. 妨害, 累赘

examples.en: Too many rules cumber the creative process.
examples.zh: 太多规则阻碍了创作过程。

examples.en: Don't cumber yourself with unnecessary worries.
examples.zh: 不要用不必要的忧虑妨碍自己。

definitions.en: s. base and cowardly
definitions.zh: a. 野狗似的, 脾气坏的, 没教养的

examples.en: His currish attitude made everyone dislike him.
examples.zh: 他野狗似的态度让每个人都不喜欢他。

examples.en: A currish person often snaps at others.
examples.zh: 一个没教养的人常常对别人发火。

definitions.en: v deaden (a sound or noise), especially by wrapping
definitions.zh: a. 被窒息的；阻尼的；衰减的

examples.en: The sound was damped by thick curtains.
examples.zh: 声音被厚窗帘衰减了。

examples.en: The vibrations were damped by the rubber mat.
examples.zh: 振动被橡胶垫阻尼了。

definitions.en: n. a despicable coward
definitions.zh: n. 懦夫, 卑鄙的人

definitions.en: s. despicably cowardly
definitions.zh: a. 怯懦的

examples.en: Only a dastard would harm a child.
examples.zh: 只有懦夫才会伤害孩子。

examples.en: He acted like a dastard in the fight.
examples.zh: 他在打斗中表现得像个懦夫。

definitions.zh: n. 拙劣的画匠

examples.en: The daubster's painting was full of mistakes.
examples.zh: 这个拙劣画匠的画满是错误。

examples.en: No one wanted to buy the daubster's art.
examples.zh: 没人想买这个拙劣画匠的艺术品。

definitions.en: v appropriate (as property entrusted to one's care) fraudulently to one's own use
definitions.zh: vi. 盗用公款, 侵吞公款
[经] 侵吞, 盗用, 贪污

examples.en: The accountant was caught trying to defalcate funds.
examples.zh: 会计被抓到试图盗用资金。

examples.en: He used his position to defalcate company money.
examples.zh: 他利用职位侵吞公司钱财。

definitions.en: n an insect that strips the leaves from plants
definitions.zh: n. 除叶剂, 食叶之昆虫

examples.en: The defoliator destroyed the farmer's crops.
examples.zh: 食叶昆虫毁坏了农民的庄稼。

examples.en: A defoliator can strip a tree in days.
examples.zh: 一种食叶昆虫能在几天内剥光一棵树。

definitions.en: v. remove the trees from
definitions.zh: vt. 滥伐森林, 砍掉...上的树林

examples.en: They plan to deforest the area for farming.
examples.zh: 他们计划砍伐这片区域的森林用于农耕。

examples.en: We should not deforest without planting new trees.
examples.zh: 我们不应该不种新树就滥伐森林。

definitions.en: v. t. To denounce; to condemn publicly or solemnly.
definitions.zh: vt. 告发, 抨击, 谴责

examples.en: The leader will denunciate the unfair policy.
examples.zh: 领导人将谴责不公平的政策。

examples.en: They denunciate corruption in the government.
examples.zh: 他们抨击政府中的腐败。

definitions.en: v move (people) forcibly from their homeland into a new and foreign environment
definitions.zh: vt. 根除, 杜绝, 使脱离传统

examples.en: The war deracinated many families from their homes.
examples.zh: 战争使许多家庭脱离家园。

examples.en: It is hard to deracinate old traditions completely.
examples.zh: 完全根除旧传统很难。

definitions.en: v remove salt from
definitions.zh: v. 除去盐分, 淡化海水

examples.en: The plant can desalinize seawater for drinking.
examples.zh: 这个工厂能淡化海水供饮用。

examples.en: They use a machine to desalinize the water.
examples.zh: 他们用一台机器除去水中的盐分。

definitions.en: v. catch sight of
definitions.zh: vt. 看出, 看见, 发现

examples.en: From the hill, he could descry the distant town.
examples.zh: 从山上，他能看见远处的城镇。

examples.en: She descried a ship on the horizon.
examples.zh: 她发现地平线上有一艘船。

definitions.en: v preserve by removing all water and liquids from
definitions.zh: vt. 使干, 干贮

definitions.en: v remove water from
definitions.zh: vi. 变干

examples.en: The sun will desiccate the wet soil quickly.
examples.zh: 太阳会很快使湿土变干。

examples.en: They desiccate fruits to preserve them for winter.
examples.zh: 他们干贮水果以备冬天食用。

definitions.en: a. easily destroyed
definitions.zh: a. 可破坏的

examples.en: Glass is a very destructible material.
examples.zh: 玻璃是一种非常可破坏的材料。

examples.en: This toy is destructible, so handle it with care.
examples.zh: 这个玩具是可破坏的，所以要小心处理。

definitions.en: n. a petty disparagement
definitions.zh: n. 转移, 缩小, 减损, 贬低, 毁损

examples.en: His constant detraction of others made him unpopular.
examples.zh: 他不断贬低别人使他不受欢迎。

examples.en: Detraction can damage a person's reputation.
examples.zh: 贬低会损害一个人的声誉。

definitions.en: v. bring into a condition of decay or partial ruin by neglect or misuse
definitions.zh: v. (使)荒废, (使)毁坏

examples.en: The old house began to dilapidate over time.
examples.zh: 老房子随着时间开始荒废。

examples.en: Neglect caused the building to dilapidate quickly.
examples.zh: 疏忽导致建筑迅速毁坏。

definitions.en: n. an intense persistent desire to drink alcoholic beverages to excess
definitions.zh: n. 嗜酒症, 饮酒狂
[医] 间发性酒狂

examples.en: His dipsomania ruined his health and family.
examples.zh: 他的嗜酒症毁了他的健康和家庭。

examples.en: Dipsomania is a serious addiction to alcohol.
examples.zh: 嗜酒症是一种严重的酒精成瘾。

definitions.en: v arouse hostility or indifference in where there had formerly been love, affection, or friendliness
definitions.zh: vt. 使疏远, 使不忠, 使不满意

examples.en: The unfair treatment began to disaffect the workers.
examples.zh: 不公平的待遇开始使工人疏远。

examples.en: His rude comments disaffect his friends.
examples.zh: 他粗鲁的评论使朋友们不满意。

definitions.en: v cause to be confused emotionally
definitions.zh: vt. 使混乱, 使困惑, 使泄气

examples.en: The sudden noise discombobulate the speaker.
examples.zh: 突然的噪音使演讲者困惑。

examples.en: Don't let small problems discombobulate you.
examples.zh: 不要让小问题使你混乱。

definitions.en: s. having self-possession upset; thrown into confusion
definitions.zh: vt. 使混乱；使泄气；使困惑

examples.en: She felt discombobulated after the long flight.
examples.zh: 长途飞行后她感到困惑。

examples.en: The unexpected question left him discombobulated.
examples.zh: 意外的问题使他混乱。

definitions.en: imp. & p. p. of Discomfit
definitions.zh: v. 使为难( discomfit的过去式和过去分词); 使狼狈; 使挫折; 挫败

examples.en: He was discomfited by the difficult question.
examples.zh: 他被这个难题弄得狼狈。

examples.en: The team felt discomfited after losing the game.
examples.zh: 输掉比赛后队伍感到挫败。

definitions.en: v cause to lose one's composure
definitions.zh: vt. 使不安, 使烦乱, 使烦恼

examples.en: The bad news discompose her greatly.
examples.zh: 坏消息使她非常不安。

examples.en: Try not to let criticism discompose you.
examples.zh: 尽量不要让批评使你烦乱。

definitions.en: v. free from enchantment
definitions.zh: vt. 使清醒

examples.en: The movie's ending disenchant many viewers.
examples.zh: 电影的结局使许多观众清醒。

examples.en: Reality can disenchant those with high hopes.
examples.zh: 现实能使抱有高希望的人清醒。

definitions.en: v deprive of voting rights
definitions.zh: vt. 剥夺公民权, 剥夺推举议员权, 夺权利
[法] 剥夺公民权, 剥夺选举权, 终止特许权

examples.en: The law tried to disfranchise minority voters.
examples.zh: 法律试图剥夺少数族裔选民的选举权。

examples.en: They fought against efforts to disfranchise citizens.
examples.zh: 他们反对剥夺公民权的努力。

definitions.en: v. put into a bad mood or into bad humour
definitions.zh: vt. 使不高兴

examples.en: The delay disgruntle the waiting passengers.
examples.zh: 延误使等待的乘客不高兴。

examples.en: Poor service can disgruntle customers easily.
examples.zh: 差的服务容易使顾客不高兴。

definitions.en: v disarrange or rumple; dishevel
definitions.zh: vt. 使蓬乱, 使头发凌乱

examples.en: The wind dishevel her hair completely.
examples.zh: 风使她的头发完全蓬乱。

examples.en: He didn't care to dishevel his neat appearance.
examples.zh: 他不在乎弄乱他整洁的外表。

definitions.en: n. any evidence that helps to establish the falsity of something
definitions.zh: n. 反证, 反驳
[法] 反证, 反证物, 反驳

examples.en: The scientist provided disproof of the old theory.
examples.zh: 科学家提供了旧理论的反证。

examples.en: There is no disproof for his claim yet.
examples.zh: 还没有对他的主张的反驳。

definitions.en: v. t. To tinge with a different color from the natural or
definitions.zh: v. 使变色,弄脏,伤害名誉

examples.en: The mud distain his white shirt badly.
examples.zh: 泥土严重弄脏了他的白衬衫。

examples.en: Scandal can distain a person's reputation forever.
examples.zh: 丑闻会永远伤害一个人的名誉。

definitions.en: s having the attention diverted especially because of anxiety
definitions.zh: a. 心不在焉的

examples.en: She looked distrait during the important meeting.
examples.zh: 她在重要会议期间显得心不在焉。

examples.en: His distrait manner worried his colleagues.
examples.zh: 他心不在焉的样子让同事担心。

definitions.en: v lose clarity or turn aside especially from the main subject of attention or course of argument in writing, thinking, or speaking
definitions.zh: v. 流浪, 漫游,离题

examples.en: The speaker began to divagate from the topic.
examples.zh: 演讲者开始偏离主题。

examples.en: Try not to divagate when writing your essay.
examples.zh: 写文章时尽量不要离题。

definitions.en: r. quietly in concealment
definitions.zh: adv. 隐秘地；躲藏地；一动也不动地

examples.en: The cat lay doggo under the bed.
examples.zh: 猫躲在床下一动也不动。

examples.en: He stayed doggo to avoid being seen.
examples.zh: 他隐秘地待着以免被发现。

definitions.en: n. a belt of calms and light winds between the northern and southern trade winds of the Atlantic and Pacific
definitions.zh: n. 忧郁, 赤道无风带

examples.en: The ship was stuck in the doldrums for days.
examples.zh: 船在赤道无风带被困了几天。

examples.en: He felt in the doldrums after the bad news.
examples.zh: 坏消息后他感到忧郁。

definitions.zh: vt. 欺骗, 出卖

examples.en: He tried to double-cross his business partner.
examples.zh: 他试图欺骗他的商业伙伴。

examples.en: Never double-cross someone who trusts you.
examples.zh: 永远不要出卖信任你的人。

definitions.en: s. sensible and practical
definitions.zh: a. 实际的

examples.en: She is a very down-to-earth person.
examples.zh: 她是一个非常实际的人。

examples.en: His down-to-earth advice helped me a lot.
examples.zh: 他实际的建议帮了我很多。

definitions.en: s. extremely pleasant in a gentle way
definitions.zh: a. 悦目的, 美妙的, 美味的, 悦耳的

examples.en: The dulcet music calmed the baby.
examples.zh: 悦耳的音乐让宝宝平静下来。

examples.en: She spoke in a dulcet tone.
examples.zh: 她用甜美的语调说话。

definitions.en: s loud enough to cause (temporary) hearing loss
definitions.zh: a. 震耳欲聋的

examples.en: The earsplitting noise hurt my ears.
examples.zh: 震耳欲聋的噪音伤了我的耳朵。

examples.en: An earsplitting siren woke everyone up.
examples.zh: 震耳欲聋的警报声吵醒了所有人。

definitions.en: s. loud enough to shake the very earth
definitions.zh: a. 惊天动地的

examples.en: The news was truly earthshaking.
examples.zh: 这个消息真是惊天动地。

examples.en: An earthshaking event changed history.
examples.zh: 一个惊天动地的事件改变了历史。

definitions.en: n periodic shedding of the cuticle in arthropods or the outer skin in reptiles
definitions.zh: n. 蜕皮, 蜕化
[医] 蜕皮, 换羽

examples.en: The snake undergoes ecdysis regularly.
examples.zh: 蛇定期蜕皮。

examples.en: Ecdysis is common in arthropods.
examples.zh: 蜕皮在节肢动物中很常见。

definitions.en: v become bubbly or frothy or foaming
definitions.zh: vi. 冒泡, 泡腾, 兴奋
[医] 起泡, 发气泡

examples.en: The soda began to effervesce.
examples.zh: 苏打水开始冒泡。

examples.en: The crowd effervesced with excitement.
examples.zh: 人群兴奋地沸腾起来。

definitions.en: s radiating or as if radiating light
definitions.zh: a. 光辉灿烂的

examples.en: The effulgent sun lit the sky.
examples.zh: 灿烂的太阳照亮了天空。

examples.en: Her smile was effulgent and warm.
examples.zh: 她的笑容灿烂而温暖。

definitions.en: s. inspiring awe
definitions.zh: a. 最高天的, 九天的, 苍天的

examples.en: The empyreal view inspired the poet.
examples.zh: 苍天的景色激发了诗人的灵感。

examples.en: He gazed at the empyreal stars.
examples.zh: 他凝视着苍天的星星。

definitions.en: a. of or relating to the sky or heavens
definitions.zh: n. 最高天, 九天, 苍天

examples.en: The empyrean realm seemed endless.
examples.zh: 苍天领域似乎无边无际。

examples.en: Birds flew in the empyrean sky.
examples.zh: 鸟儿在苍天中飞翔。

definitions.en: v convert ordinary language into code
definitions.zh: vt. 译成密码
[计] 编码

examples.en: The spy had to encipher the message.
examples.zh: 间谍必须将信息译成密码。

examples.en: Learn how to encipher data securely.
examples.zh: 学习如何安全地编码数据。

definitions.en: n. One who praises; a panegyrist.
definitions.zh: n. 宣读或写作颂辞之人, 赞美者, 阿谀者

examples.en: The encomiast praised the hero's deeds.
examples.zh: 赞美者颂扬英雄的事迹。

examples.en: An encomiast spoke at the ceremony.
examples.zh: 一位赞美者在典礼上发言。

definitions.en: v give qualities or abilities to
definitions.zh: vt. 授予, 赋予, 穿上

examples.en: Nature endues us with talents.
examples.zh: 自然赋予我们才能。

examples.en: The king endued him with power.
examples.zh: 国王授予他权力。

definitions.en: v. t. To bind in fetters; to enchain.
definitions.zh: vt. 给...上脚镣, 束缚, 使受制于

examples.en: The chains enfetter the prisoner.
examples.zh: 锁链束缚了囚犯。

examples.en: Don't let fear enfetter your mind.
examples.zh: 不要让恐惧束缚你的思想。

definitions.zh: v. 燃烧

examples.en: The fire began to enflame the wood.
examples.zh: 火开始燃烧木头。

examples.en: His words enflame the crowd's anger.
examples.zh: 他的话点燃了人群的愤怒。

definitions.en: n complete attention; intense mental effort
definitions.zh: n. 正式缮写的文件,专注

examples.en: Her engrossment in the book was total.
examples.zh: 她完全专注于那本书。

examples.en: Engrossment in work helps him relax.
examples.zh: 专注于工作帮助他放松。

definitions.en: v extend on all sides of simultaneously; encircle
definitions.zh: vt. 包围, 环绕

examples.en: The forest environs the small lake.
examples.zh: 森林环绕着小湖。

examples.en: Mountains environ the peaceful valley.
examples.zh: 群山环绕着宁静的山谷。

definitions.en: s formally expressing praise
definitions.zh: a. 颂扬的, 歌功颂德的, 称赞的

examples.en: The speech was very eulogistic.
examples.zh: 演讲非常颂扬。

examples.en: She gave a eulogistic tribute to him.
examples.zh: 她向他致以颂扬的敬意。

definitions.en: s not easily irritated
definitions.zh: a. 性情平和的

examples.en: He is an even-tempered person.
examples.zh: 他是一个性情平和的人。

examples.en: Stay even-tempered during the debate.
examples.zh: 在辩论中保持平和。

definitions.en: s. without partiality
definitions.zh: a. 公平的, 公平无私的

examples.en: The judge was evenhanded in court.
examples.zh: 法官在法庭上公平无私。

examples.en: An evenhanded policy benefits everyone.
examples.zh: 公平的政策惠及所有人。

definitions.en: s. liable to objection or debate; used of something one might take exception to
definitions.zh: a. 可反对的, 可抗议的

examples.en: His comment was highly exceptionable.
examples.zh: 他的评论非常可反对。

examples.en: The clause in the contract is exceptionable.
examples.zh: 合同中的条款可反对。

definitions.en: v come up with (an idea, plan, explanation, theory, or principle) after a mental effort
definitions.zh: vt. 想出, 研究出, 设计, 发明

examples.en: He excogitated a new plan.
examples.zh: 他想出了一个新计划。

examples.en: She excogitated a clever solution.
examples.zh: 她设计了一个聪明的解决方案。

definitions.en: v torment emotionally or mentally
definitions.zh: vt. 施酷刑, 拷问, 使苦恼, 折磨

examples.en: The pain excruciates him daily.
examples.zh: 疼痛每天折磨着他。

examples.en: Guilt can excruciate the mind.
examples.zh: 内疚会折磨心灵。

definitions.en: s (of e.g. speech and writing) tending to depart from the main point or cover a wide range of subjects
definitions.zh: a. 游览的, 离题的, 散漫的
[医] 移动性的

examples.en: His excursive speech confused the audience.
examples.zh: 他离题的演讲让听众困惑。

examples.en: The essay was too excursive.
examples.zh: 这篇文章太散漫了。

definitions.en: v find repugnant
definitions.zh: vt. 憎恨, 憎恶, 诅咒

definitions.en: v curse or declare to be evil or anathema or threaten with divine punishment
definitions.zh: vi. 诅咒

examples.en: They execrate violence in any form.
examples.zh: 他们憎恨任何形式的暴力。

examples.en: The crowd execrated the traitor.
examples.zh: 人群诅咒那个叛徒。

definitions.en: n. an appeal to some supernatural power to inflict evil on someone or some group
definitions.zh: n. 憎恶, 诅咒, 被咒骂的人(或事)

examples.en: He muttered an execration under his breath.
examples.zh: 他低声咒骂。

examples.en: The execration of the villain was loud.
examples.zh: 对恶棍的诅咒很响亮。

definitions.en: v. fill with sublime emotion
definitions.zh: vt. 使高兴, 使愉快, 鼓励

examples.en: The good news exhilarated everyone.
examples.zh: 好消息使每个人高兴。

examples.en: A walk in nature can exhilarate you.
examples.zh: 在大自然中散步能让你愉快。

definitions.en: v edit by omitting or modifying parts considered indelicate
definitions.zh: vt. 删除, 修订, 使纯洁

examples.en: The editor expurgated the offensive parts.
examples.zh: 编辑删除了冒犯的部分。

examples.en: They expurgated the book for children.
examples.zh: 他们为儿童修订了这本书。

definitions.en: v manage in a makeshift way; do with whatever is at hand
definitions.zh: v. 即席演说, 即兴演奏, 当场作成

examples.en: He had to extemporize a speech.
examples.zh: 他必须即席演说。

examples.en: The musician extemporized a beautiful tune.
examples.zh: 音乐家即兴演奏了一首优美的曲子。

definitions.en: a. capable of being extricated
definitions.zh: a. 可救出的, 可解救的

examples.en: The problem is not easily extricable.
examples.zh: 这个问题不容易解救。

examples.en: Is the knot extricable from the rope?
examples.zh: 这个结能从绳子上解开吗？

definitions.en: n a building or place that provides a particular service or is used for a particular industry
definitions.zh: n. 工具, 设施, 设备

examples.en: The school has modern facilities.
examples.zh: 学校有现代化的设施。

examples.en: Public facilities are well maintained.
examples.zh: 公共设施维护得很好。

definitions.zh: [计] 可分解因子的

examples.en: This equation is factorable.
examples.zh: 这个方程可分解因式。

examples.en: Is the polynomial factorable?
examples.zh: 这个多项式可分解因式吗？

definitions.en: n. a mechanism capable of returning to a safe state in case there is a failure or malfunction
definitions.zh: n. 自动防故障装置

definitions.en: s. guaranteed not to fail
definitions.zh: a. 自动防故障装置的

definitions.en: s. eliminating danger by compensating automatically for a failure or malfunction
definitions.zh: [计] 故障保险

examples.en: The system has a fail-safe mechanism.
examples.zh: 系统有自动防故障装置。

examples.en: This design is fail-safe and reliable.
examples.zh: 这个设计是自动防故障且可靠的。

definitions.en: s lacking conviction or boldness or courage
definitions.zh: a. 懦弱的, 无精神的, 胆小的

examples.en: He is too fainthearted to try.
examples.zh: 他太胆小不敢尝试。

examples.en: Fainthearted people avoid risks.
examples.zh: 胆小的人避免风险。

definitions.en: v be hungry; go without food
definitions.zh: vt. 使挨饿

definitions.en: v deprive of food
definitions.zh: vi. 饥饿, 挨饿

examples.en: The prisoners began to famish.
examples.zh: 囚犯们开始挨饿。

examples.en: Do not famish the animals.
examples.zh: 不要让动物挨饿。

definitions.zh: a. 深远的, 广泛的, 伸至远处的

examples.en: The decision had far-reaching effects.
examples.zh: 这个决定有深远的影响。

examples.en: Her research has far-reaching implications.
examples.zh: 她的研究有广泛的意义。

definitions.en: n a ludicrous folly
definitions.zh: n. 愚钝, 昏庸, 愚蠢言行
[医] 愚昧

examples.en: His fatuity amazed everyone.
examples.zh: 他的愚钝让所有人惊讶。

examples.en: Don't listen to such fatuity.
examples.zh: 别听这种愚蠢的言论。

definitions.en: n someone who is critical of the motives of others
definitions.zh: n. 吹毛求疵的人

examples.en: He is a constant faultfinder.
examples.zh: 他是一个经常吹毛求疵的人。

examples.en: The faultfinder criticized everything.
examples.zh: 吹毛求疵的人批评一切。

definitions.en: v express congratulations
definitions.zh: vt. 庆祝, 庆贺

examples.en: I felicitate you on your success.
examples.zh: 我祝贺你的成功。

examples.en: They felicitated the happy couple.
examples.zh: 他们祝贺这对幸福的情侣。

definitions.en: s offering fun and gaiety
definitions.zh: a. 节日的, 祭日的, 欢乐的

examples.en: The festal atmosphere was joyful.
examples.zh: 节日的气氛很欢乐。

examples.en: We enjoyed a festal dinner together.
examples.zh: 我们一起享受了欢乐的晚餐。

definitions.en: n the entering of a legal document into the public record
definitions.zh: n. 锉屑

definitions.en: n a fragment rubbed off by the use of a file
definitions.zh: [医] 锉屑

examples.en: Metal filings covered the floor.
examples.zh: 金属锉屑覆盖了地板。

examples.en: The court received the legal filings.
examples.zh: 法院收到了法律文件归档。

definitions.en: s. liable to a fine
definitions.zh: a. 应罚款的
[法] 可罚款的, 该罚款的

examples.en: This offense is finable by law.
examples.zh: 这种违法行为应罚款。

examples.en: Parking here is finable.
examples.zh: 在这里停车应罚款。

definitions.en: a. Weak; flexible; limber.
definitions.zh: a. 多扁石的, 多菖蒲的, 凋萎的, 松软的

examples.en: The old rope felt flaggy and weak.
examples.zh: 旧绳子感觉松软无力。

examples.en: His flaggy arms could not lift the box.
examples.zh: 他无力的手臂抬不起箱子。

definitions.en: n. freight car without permanent sides or roof
definitions.zh: n. 平板货车, 平板车

examples.en: The train had a flatcar for lumber.
examples.zh: 火车有一节运木材的平板车。

examples.en: They loaded the flatcar with steel beams.
examples.zh: 他们把钢梁装上了平板货车。

definitions.en: s inclined to flaunt
definitions.zh: a. 虚华的

examples.en: Her flaunty dress attracted everyone's attention.
examples.zh: 她虚华的裙子吸引了所有人的注意。

examples.en: He gave a flaunty wave to the crowd.
examples.zh: 他向人群虚华地挥了挥手。

definitions.en: v. act foolishly, as by talking nonsense
definitions.zh: n. 废话, 傻话, 愚蠢的做法, 呓语, 呆话
vi. 说呆话, 做笨事

examples.en: Stop your footle and get to work.
examples.zh: 别再说傻话了，开始工作吧。

examples.en: His speech was full of footle.
examples.zh: 他的演讲充满了废话。

definitions.en: v make a prediction about; tell in advance
definitions.zh: v. 预示, 预兆, 预感

examples.en: Dark clouds forebode a coming storm.
examples.zh: 乌云预示着一场暴风雨即将来临。

examples.en: His silence seemed to forebode trouble.
examples.zh: 他的沉默似乎预示着麻烦。

definitions.en: n. a bed with posts at the four corners that can be used to support a canopy or curtains
definitions.zh: n. 四柱大型卧床

examples.en: She slept in a beautiful four-poster bed.
examples.zh: 她睡在一张漂亮的四柱床上。

examples.en: The antique four-poster was very expensive.
examples.zh: 那张古董四柱卧床非常昂贵。

definitions.en: s negligent of neatness especially in dress and person; habitually dirty and unkempt
definitions.zh: a. 不整洁的, 有臭味的, 很闷的

examples.en: The room smelled frowzy and stale.
examples.zh: 房间里有股发霉的臭味。

examples.en: He looked frowzy in his wrinkled shirt.
examples.zh: 他穿着皱巴巴的衬衫，显得不整洁。

definitions.en: v. become productive or fruitful
definitions.zh: vi. 结果实

definitions.en: v. make productive or fruitful
definitions.zh: vt. 使结果实, 使肥沃

examples.en: The apple tree will fructify in autumn.
examples.zh: 苹果树将在秋天结果实。

examples.en: Hard work will fructify your efforts.
examples.zh: 努力工作将使你的努力结出果实。

definitions.en: s. fully ripe; at the height of bloom
definitions.zh: a. 盛开的, 成熟的, (帆等)满张的

examples.en: The rose is now full-blown and beautiful.
examples.zh: 玫瑰现在盛开了，非常美丽。

examples.en: The crisis became a full-blown disaster.
examples.zh: 危机演变成了一场成熟的灾难。

definitions.en: s. marked by richness and fullness of flavor
definitions.zh: a. 肥胖的, 魁梧的, 浓郁的, 范围广的

examples.en: This wine has a full-bodied flavor.
examples.zh: 这款酒有浓郁的风味。

examples.en: She prefers full-bodied red wines.
examples.zh: 她更喜欢浓郁的红酒。

definitions.en: s. (of a bird) having reached full development with fully grown adult plumage; ready to fly
definitions.zh: a. 羽毛生齐的, 发育完全的, 有充分资格的

examples.en: The bird is now a full-fledged adult.
examples.zh: 这只鸟现在已发育完全。

examples.en: She became a full-fledged doctor last year.
examples.zh: 她去年成了一名有充分资格的医生。

definitions.en: n. the taxonomic kingdom including yeast, molds, smuts, mushrooms, and toadstools; distinct from the green plants
definitions.zh: pl. 真菌, 突然发生而迅速生长的东西
[医] 真菌, 霉菌, 蕈, 海绵肿

examples.en: Mushrooms are a type of fungi.
examples.zh: 蘑菇是真菌的一种。

examples.en: Fungi grow in damp and dark places.
examples.zh: 真菌生长在潮湿阴暗的地方。

definitions.en: v polish and make shiny
definitions.zh: vt. 擦亮, 研磨, 磨光

examples.en: He furbished the old silver spoon.
examples.zh: 他擦亮了那把旧银勺。

examples.en: She furbished her shoes until they shone.
examples.zh: 她把鞋子擦得锃亮。

definitions.en: n. the quality of being wordy and talkative
definitions.zh: n. 饶舌, 多嘴
[医] 多言

examples.en: His garrulity made the meeting too long.
examples.zh: 他的饶舌使会议拖得太长。

examples.en: I avoid her because of her garrulity.
examples.zh: 我因为她多嘴而避开她。

definitions.en: n the quality of being rustic or gauche
definitions.zh: n. 笨拙, 不老练, 无礼

examples.en: His gaucherie at the party was embarrassing.
examples.zh: 他在聚会上的笨拙令人尴尬。

examples.en: She apologized for her gaucherie.
examples.zh: 她为自己的无礼道歉。

definitions.en: n a mathematician specializing in geometry
definitions.zh: n. 几何学者

examples.en: The geometrician solved the complex problem.
examples.zh: 几何学者解决了那个复杂问题。

examples.en: She is a famous geometrician at the university.
examples.zh: 她是大学里一位著名的几何学者。

definitions.en: n an agent (as heat or radiation or a chemical) that destroys microorganisms that might carry disease
definitions.zh: n. 杀菌剂
[化] 杀菌剂

examples.en: The doctor used a germicide to clean the wound.
examples.zh: 医生用杀菌剂清洗伤口。

examples.en: This germicide kills most bacteria quickly.
examples.zh: 这种杀菌剂能迅速杀死大多数细菌。

definitions.en: n. a soldier who performs his duties without proper care or effort
definitions.zh: vi. 逃避工作, 游手好闲

definitions.en: n. an idle worthless person
definitions.zh: n. 假金砖, 赝品, 懒汉

examples.en: He is a goldbrick who avoids all work.
examples.zh: 他是个逃避所有工作的懒汉。

examples.en: Don't be a goldbrick; help your team.
examples.zh: 别游手好闲，帮帮你的团队。

definitions.en: v overeat or eat immodestly; make a pig of oneself
definitions.zh: v. 狼吞虎咽
n. 讲究饮食, 大吃大喝

examples.en: He tends to gormandize at every meal.
examples.zh: 他每顿饭都狼吞虎咽。

examples.en: Don't gormandize; eat slowly and enjoy.
examples.zh: 别大吃大喝，慢慢吃，享受食物。

definitions.en: n the faculty of distinguishing sweet, sour, bitter, and salty properties in the mouth
definitions.zh: n. 尝味, 味觉
[医] 味觉, 尝味

examples.en: Gustation is the sense of taste.
examples.zh: 味觉就是品尝味道的能力。

examples.en: Her gustation is very sensitive to spices.
examples.zh: 她的味觉对香料非常敏感。

definitions.en: v eat greedily
definitions.zh: v. 狼吞虎咽地吃喝

examples.en: The hungry dog guttled its food quickly.
examples.zh: 饿狗狼吞虎咽地吃完了食物。

examples.en: He guttled the cake in just two bites.
examples.zh: 他两口就狼吞虎咽地吃掉了蛋糕。

definitions.zh: n. 妇女当政, 女权政治

examples.en: The ancient society was a gynaecocracy.
examples.zh: 那个古代社会是妇女当政的。

examples.en: Gynaecocracy is rare in modern history.
examples.zh: 女权政治在现代历史上很少见。

definitions.en: s. feeling or showing little interest or enthusiasm
definitions.zh: a. 不认真的, 无兴趣的, 不热心的

examples.en: He gave a halfhearted effort to the task.
examples.zh: 他对这项任务只付出了不认真的努力。

examples.en: Her halfhearted smile showed no real joy.
examples.zh: 她不认真的微笑没有显示出真正的快乐。

definitions.zh: a. 顽强的, 坚韧的

examples.en: The hardbitten soldier never gave up.
examples.zh: 那位顽强的士兵从不放弃。

examples.en: She is a hardbitten negotiator in business.
examples.zh: 她在生意场上是一位坚韧的谈判者。

definitions.en: s. unreasonably rigid in the face of argument or entreaty or attack
definitions.zh: a. 不易激动的, 冷静的, 脚踏实地的, 无懈可击的

examples.en: He is hardheaded and refuses to listen.
examples.zh: 他固执己见，拒绝听取意见。

examples.en: A hardheaded approach can solve this problem.
examples.zh: 冷静务实的方法可以解决这个问题。

definitions.en: n the trait of being willing to undertake things that involve risk or danger
definitions.zh: n. 胆大无敌, 刚毅, 厚颜, 强壮

examples.en: His hardihood helped him climb the mountain.
examples.zh: 他的刚毅帮助他爬上了山。

examples.en: She showed great hardihood in the crisis.
examples.zh: 她在危机中表现出了极大的胆量。

definitions.en: s causing or marked by grief or anguish
definitions.zh: a. 令人心碎的, 悲惨的

examples.en: The movie had a heartrending ending.
examples.zh: 这部电影有一个令人心碎的结局。

examples.en: Her heartrending story made everyone cry.
examples.zh: 她悲惨的故事让每个人都哭了。

definitions.zh: 笨手笨脚的

examples.en: His heavy-handedness broke the delicate vase.
examples.zh: 他的笨手笨脚打碎了那个精致的花瓶。

examples.en: The manager's heavy-handedness upset the staff.
examples.zh: 经理的笨拙处理让员工不满。

definitions.en: n (Middle Ages) a person who is bound to the land and owned by the feudal lord
definitions.zh: n. 希洛人(古斯巴达奴隶), 奴隶, 农奴

examples.en: In ancient Sparta, a helot was a slave.
examples.zh: 在古斯巴达，希洛人是奴隶。

examples.en: The helot worked in the fields all day.
examples.zh: 那个农奴整天在田里干活。

definitions.en: n the handle of a weapon or tool
definitions.zh: n. 柄
vt. 装柄于

examples.en: The axe helve was made of strong wood.
examples.zh: 斧柄是用结实的木头做的。

examples.en: He replaced the broken helve on the hammer.
examples.zh: 他更换了锤子上断裂的柄。

definitions.en: n. a surgical instrument that stops bleeding by clamping the blood vessel
definitions.zh: n. 止血钳子, 止血剂
[医] 止血器, 止血剂

examples.en: The surgeon used a hemostat to stop bleeding.
examples.zh: 外科医生用止血钳止血。

examples.en: A hemostat is essential in any surgery.
examples.zh: 止血钳在任何手术中都是必需的。

definitions.en: s harassed by persistent nagging
definitions.zh: a. 怕老婆的, 惧内的, 老婆当家的

examples.en: He is a henpecked husband who obeys his wife.
examples.zh: 他是个怕老婆的丈夫，听妻子的话。

examples.en: The henpecked man never makes his own decisions.
examples.zh: 那个惧内的男人从不自己做决定。

definitions.en: n. two words are homographs if they are spelled the same way but differ in meaning (e.g. fair)
definitions.zh: n. 同形异义字

examples.en: The word 'lead' is a homograph with two meanings.
examples.zh: 单词'lead'是一个同形异义词，有两个意思。

examples.en: Homographs can confuse language learners.
examples.zh: 同形异义词可能会让语言学习者困惑。

definitions.en: n. the art of designing and making clocks
definitions.zh: n. 测时法, 钟表制造术

examples.en: He studied horology to make better clocks.
examples.zh: 他学习钟表制造术以制作更好的钟。

examples.en: Horology is the art of designing clocks.
examples.zh: 测时法是设计钟表的艺术。

definitions.en: s giving strong encouragement
definitions.zh: a. 劝告的, 奖励的

examples.en: Her hortative speech inspired the team.
examples.zh: 她劝告性的演讲激励了团队。

examples.en: He gave hortative advice to the students.
examples.zh: 他给了学生们鼓励性的建议。

definitions.en: v. i. To worship idols; to pay idolatrous worship.
definitions.zh: vt. 把…奉为偶像；盲目崇拜

examples.en: Some people idolatrize celebrities too much.
examples.zh: 有些人过度盲目崇拜名人。

examples.en: Don't idolatrize wealth; it's not everything.
examples.zh: 别把财富奉为偶像，它不是一切。

definitions.en: v. be imminent or about to happen
definitions.zh: vi. 迫近, 威胁, 悬挂

examples.en: A storm seems to impend over the city.
examples.zh: 一场暴风雨似乎即将降临城市。

examples.en: Danger may impend if we are not careful.
examples.zh: 如果我们不小心，危险可能迫近。

definitions.en: a. not penitent or remorseful
definitions.zh: a. 不知悔改的, 顽固的

definitions.en: s. impervious to moral persuasion
definitions.zh: n. 不知悔改的人, 顽固的人

examples.en: The impenitent thief showed no regret.
examples.zh: 那个不知悔改的小偷没有表现出悔意。

examples.en: He remained impenitent despite the evidence.
examples.zh: 尽管有证据，他仍然顽固不化。

definitions.en: n powerlessness revealed by an inability to act
definitions.zh: n. 无力, 虚弱, 无能

examples.en: His impuissance left him unable to act.
examples.zh: 他的无能使他无法行动。

examples.en: The team's impuissance led to their defeat.
examples.zh: 团队的无力导致了他们的失败。

definitions.en: s. too small to make a significant difference
definitions.zh: a. 微不足道的

examples.en: The difference in price is inappreciable.
examples.zh: 价格上的差异微不足道。

examples.en: An inappreciable amount of dust settled.
examples.zh: 微不足道的灰尘落了下来。

definitions.en: n the state of being unsure of something
definitions.zh: n. 不确实, 无信心, 不安全

examples.en: His incertitude made him hesitate.
examples.zh: 他的不确定使他犹豫。

examples.en: She felt incertitude about the future.
examples.zh: 她对未来感到不确定。

definitions.en: a. Toughtless; inconsiderate.
definitions.zh: a. 无思想的；粗心的；不体谅的

examples.en: His incogitant remark hurt her feelings.
examples.zh: 他无思想的言论伤害了她的感情。

examples.en: An incogitant driver caused the accident.
examples.zh: 一个粗心的司机导致了事故。

definitions.en: n. The state or quality of being incorrigible.
definitions.zh: n. 屡教不改, 难望矫正

examples.en: His incorrigibility frustrated his teachers.
examples.zh: 他的屡教不改让老师很沮丧。

examples.en: The child's incorrigibility worried his parents.
examples.zh: 孩子的难望矫正让父母担忧。

definitions.en: n. the formation of a crust
definitions.zh: n. 用硬壳包, 镶嵌, 痂, 硬壳

definitions.en: n. a decorative coating of contrasting material that is applied to a surface as an inlay or overlay
definitions.zh: [医] 结痂, 痂

examples.en: The incrustation on the pipe was thick.
examples.zh: 管道上的硬壳很厚。

examples.en: The wall had a beautiful incrustation of marble.
examples.zh: 墙上有一层漂亮的大理石镶嵌。

definitions.en: v suggest that someone is guilty
definitions.zh: vt. 使负罪, 控告, 使连累
[法] 控告, 连累, 归罪于

examples.en: The evidence will inculpate the suspect.
examples.zh: 证据将使嫌疑人负罪。

examples.en: He tried to inculpate his friend.
examples.zh: 他试图连累他的朋友。

definitions.en: n a numerical scale used to compare variables with one another or with some reference number
definitions.zh: pl. 索引, 指针, 指数, 指标

examples.en: The indices show economic growth.
examples.zh: 这些指数显示经济增长。

examples.en: We use indices to compare prices.
examples.zh: 我们用指标来比较价格。

definitions.en: v produce a literary work
definitions.zh: vt. 写成文章, 创作

examples.en: She will indite a poem for the contest.
examples.zh: 她将为比赛创作一首诗。

examples.en: He indited a letter to his friend.
examples.zh: 他写了一封信给朋友。

definitions.en: v. become fixed or established
definitions.zh: vt. 使硬化, 使无感觉, 使确立
a. 顽固的, 冷酷的

examples.en: The clay will indurate in the sun.
examples.zh: 粘土在阳光下会硬化。

examples.en: His heart began to indurate over time.
examples.zh: 他的心随时间变得冷酷。

definitions.en: n a chronic drinker
definitions.zh: a. 酒醉的

definitions.en: v fill with sublime emotion
definitions.zh: n. 酒鬼

definitions.en: v make drunk (with alcoholic drinks)
definitions.zh: vt. 使醉, 使陶醉

examples.en: The inebriate stumbled down the street.
examples.zh: 那个酒鬼在街上跌跌撞撞。

examples.en: The music seemed to inebriate the crowd.
examples.zh: 音乐似乎让人群陶醉。

definitions.en: a. Incapable of being effaced; indelible; ineradicable.
definitions.zh: a. 不能消除的, 不能抹掉的

examples.en: The memory left an ineffaceable mark.
examples.zh: 记忆留下了不能消除的痕迹。

examples.en: Her smile was ineffaceable in my mind.
examples.zh: 她的微笑在我心中不能抹掉。

definitions.en: n. the lack of elasticity
definitions.zh: n. 无弹力, 生硬, 不适应性
[化] 非弹性

examples.en: The inelasticity of the rubber made it useless.
examples.zh: 橡胶的无弹力使它没用。

examples.en: His inelasticity of thought hindered progress.
examples.zh: 他思想的不适应性阻碍了进步。

definitions.en: a. not suitable or advisable
definitions.zh: a. 不便的, 不适当的, 失策的

examples.en: It is inexpedient to travel in this weather.
examples.zh: 在这种天气旅行是不适当的。

examples.en: His decision was inexpedient for the team.
examples.zh: 他的决定对团队来说失策了。

definitions.en: s. incapable of being atoned for
definitions.zh: a. 不能抵偿的, 不能平息的

examples.en: The crime was considered inexpiable.
examples.zh: 这罪行被认为不能抵偿。

examples.en: His guilt was inexpiable in her eyes.
examples.zh: 他的罪过在她眼中不能平息。

definitions.en: v. arouse unreasoning love or passion in and cause to behave in an irrational way
definitions.zh: vt. 使迷恋, 使糊涂
a. 着迷的
n. 迷恋者

examples.en: She began to infatuate him with her charm.
examples.zh: 她开始用魅力使他迷恋。

examples.en: Don't let money infatuate your judgment.
examples.zh: 别让金钱使你的判断糊涂。

definitions.en: a. not appropriate in application; defective
definitions.zh: a. 不幸的, 不完善的, 不适当的

examples.en: His infelicitous comment upset everyone.
examples.zh: 他不适当的评论让所有人不安。

examples.en: The timing of the joke was infelicitous.
examples.zh: 这个笑话的时机不恰当。

definitions.en: n. inappropriate and unpleasing manner or style (especially manner or style of expression)
definitions.zh: n. 不幸, 不适当

examples.en: The speech was full of infelicity.
examples.zh: 演讲充满了不适当之处。

examples.en: His infelicity in expression caused confusion.
examples.zh: 他表达的不适当引起了困惑。

definitions.en: a. devoid of feeling and consciousness and animation
definitions.zh: a. 无知觉的, 无生命的

examples.en: A rock is an insentient object.
examples.zh: 石头是无知觉的物体。

examples.en: The machine is insentient and cannot feel pain.
examples.zh: 机器是无生命的，不能感受疼痛。

definitions.en: v expose to the rays of the sun or affect by exposure to the sun
definitions.zh: vt. 使曝晒

examples.en: They insolate the fruits to dry them.
examples.zh: 他们曝晒水果以使其干燥。

examples.en: The farmer will insolate the hay.
examples.zh: 农夫将曝晒干草。

definitions.en: n. the quality of being intangible and not perceptible by touch
definitions.zh: n. 不可触知性, 不能把握, 难以理解

examples.en: The intangibility of love makes it hard to define.
examples.zh: 爱的不可触知性使其难以定义。

examples.en: He struggled with the intangibility of the concept.
examples.zh: 他难以理解这个概念。

definitions.en: v. encroach on the rights of others, as in trading without a proper license
definitions.zh: vi. 闯入, 干涉, 无执照营业
[法] 侵占他人权益, 无执照营业

examples.en: He tried to interlope in their conversation.
examples.zh: 他试图闯入他们的谈话。

examples.en: The company was accused of interloping.
examples.zh: 该公司被指控无执照营业。

definitions.en: n. swelling up with blood or other fluids (as with congestion)
definitions.zh: n. 膨胀, 肿大

definitions.en: n. the increase in volume of certain substances when they are heated (often accompanied by release of water)
definitions.zh: [医] 肿大, 膨大, 隆起

examples.en: The intumescence on his leg was painful.
examples.zh: 他腿上的肿大很疼。

examples.en: The intumescence of the wood was due to heat.
examples.zh: 木头的膨胀是由于热量。

definitions.en: v cause to accept or become hardened to; habituate
definitions.zh: a. 习惯的, 坚强的

examples.en: He became inured to the cold weather.
examples.zh: 他习惯了寒冷的天气。

examples.en: She was inured to hard work.
examples.zh: 她习惯了艰苦的工作。

definitions.en: v. watch over (students taking an exam, to prevent cheating)
definitions.zh: vi. 看守, 监考

examples.en: The teacher will invigilate the exam.
examples.zh: 老师将监考。

examples.en: She was asked to invigilate the test.
examples.zh: 她被要求监考。

definitions.zh: a. 不能根除的

examples.en: The habit was irradicable despite efforts.
examples.zh: 尽管努力，这习惯不能根除。

examples.en: His love for her seemed irradicable.
examples.zh: 他对她的爱似乎不能根除。

definitions.en: s lacking in nutritive value
definitions.zh: a. 贫弱的, 不毛的, 无味干燥的, 不成熟的

examples.en: The meal was jejune and unsatisfying.
examples.zh: 这顿饭贫弱且不令人满意。

examples.en: His jejune argument failed to convince anyone.
examples.zh: 他无味的论点未能说服任何人。

definitions.en: s. characterized by jokes and good humor
definitions.zh: a. 爱开玩笑的, 打趣的, 说着玩的, 滑稽的, 逗趣的, 好笑的

examples.en: His jesting tone made everyone laugh.
examples.zh: 他打趣的语气让所有人笑。

examples.en: She was jesting when she said that.
examples.zh: 她说那话时是说着玩的。

definitions.en: s full of or showing high-spirited merriment
definitions.zh: a. 欢乐的, 高兴的

examples.en: The jocund crowd celebrated the festival.
examples.zh: 欢乐的人群庆祝节日。

examples.en: Her jocund mood lifted everyone's spirits.
examples.zh: 她高兴的心情提振了大家的精神。

definitions.en: n. good judgment
definitions.zh: n. 明智

examples.en: His judiciousness helped solve the problem.
examples.zh: 他的明智帮助解决了问题。

examples.en: She showed great judiciousness in her decision.
examples.zh: 她在决定中展现了极大的明智。

definitions.en: n. the (technical) knowledge and skill required to do something
definitions.zh: n. 实际知识, 技术秘诀, 诀窍
[计] 技术诀窍

examples.en: He has the know-how to fix the car.
examples.zh: 他有修理汽车的技术秘诀。

examples.en: The company needs technical know-how.
examples.zh: 公司需要技术诀窍。

definitions.en: s showing sorrow
definitions.zh: a. 爱哭的, 悲哀的

examples.en: The lachrymose movie made her cry.
examples.zh: 悲哀的电影让她哭了。

examples.en: He was lachrymose after the sad news.
examples.zh: 听到悲伤的消息后他爱哭。

definitions.en: n. slowness by virtue of being leisurely
definitions.zh: n. 悠然, 从容

examples.en: She walked with leisureliness in the park.
examples.zh: 她悠然地在公园里走。

examples.en: His leisureliness annoyed the impatient boss.
examples.zh: 他的从容让不耐烦的老板恼火。

definitions.en: s exercising or showing good judgment
definitions.zh: a. 稳健的, 头脑冷静的；明智的

examples.en: A levelheaded person makes good decisions.
examples.zh: 头脑冷静的人做出好决定。

examples.en: She remained levelheaded during the crisis.
examples.zh: 她在危机中保持明智。

definitions.en: a. sanctioned by custom or morality especially sexual morality
definitions.zh: a. 合法的, 正当的
[法] 合法的, 正当的

examples.en: The business was licit and above board.
examples.zh: 这生意是合法的且光明正大。

examples.en: They engaged in licit activities only.
examples.zh: 他们只从事正当的活动。

definitions.en: s. consisting of or containing lignin or xylem

definitions.en: v add details, as to an account or idea; clarify the meaning of and discourse in a learned way, usually in writing

examples.zh: 有斑点的表面需要清洁。

examples.zh: 他夸张的演讲给观众留下了印象。

examples.en: She used magniloquent words to describe her success.
examples.zh: 她用夸张的词语描述自己的成功。

definitions.en: n. a distinctive odor that is offensively unpleasant

definitions.zh: vt. 解放, 释放

examples.zh: 善良的主人决定解放他的奴隶。

examples.zh: 他们为解放所有俘虏而战斗。

definitions.en: v. raid and rove in search of booty
definitions.zh: v. 劫掠, 掠夺, 袭击

examples.zh: 士兵们会在夜间劫掠村庄。

definitions.en: n. the branch of physics concerned with the motion of bodies in a frame of reference

examples.zh: 力学是物理学的一个分支。

definitions.en: a. properly deserved

examples.zh: 催眠术帮助他深度放松。

examples.zh: 这匹精神饱满的马跑得非常快。

definitions.en: s threatening or foreshadowing evil or tragic developments

examples.zh: 她写了会议记录。

examples.zh: 会议记录得到了所有人的批准。

examples.zh: 厌婚症是一种罕见但真实的感觉。

definitions.en: v time incorrectly

examples.zh: 记忆术帮助我记住新单词。

examples.en: She used mnemonics for the history test.
examples.zh: 她用记忆术准备历史考试。

definitions.en: n. a mania restricted to one thing or idea
definitions.zh: n. 狂热, 偏执狂

examples.zh: 他对工作的偏执让家人担心。

examples.zh: 偏执狂可以让人非常专注。

definitions.en: v. impose a fine on

examples.en: She criticized his pharisaic piety.

examples.zh: 他演讲的简洁有力给所有人留下了印象。

definitions.en: a. capable of being weighed or considered

examples.zh: 木刨花覆盖了车间地板。

examples.en: He cleaned up the shavings after shaving.
examples.zh: 他剃须后清理了剃须屑。

definitions.en: n. The quality or state of being shifty.
definitions.zh: 奸诈

examples.en: His shiftiness made people distrust him.
examples.zh: 他的奸诈让人们不信任他。

examples.en: Shiftiness in his eyes revealed his lie.
examples.zh: 他眼中的奸诈暴露了他的谎言。

definitions.en: n. a woman who tells fortunes
definitions.zh: n. 女巫, 女算命者, 女预言家

examples.en: The sibyl predicted the future for the king.
examples.zh: 女巫为国王预言了未来。

examples.en: People visited the sibyl for advice on love.
examples.zh: 人们拜访女算命者寻求爱情建议。

definitions.en: s very funny
definitions.zh: a. 令人捧腹大笑的

examples.en: The comedian told a sidesplitting joke last night.
examples.zh: 喜剧演员昨晚讲了一个令人捧腹大笑的笑话。

examples.en: Her sidesplitting story made everyone cry with laughter.
examples.zh: 她令人捧腹大笑的故事让每个人都笑出了泪。

definitions.zh: n. 极烫的东西, 炎热天

examples.en: Today is a real sizzler with high heat.
examples.zh: 今天真是个炎热天，温度很高。

examples.en: The steak on the grill is a sizzler.
examples.zh: 烤架上的牛排是极烫的东西。

definitions.en: r. in a careless or reckless manner
definitions.zh: n. 草率
a. 猛烈的, 粗心的

examples.en: He did a slapdash job on the report.
examples.zh: 他草草地完成了报告。

examples.en: Her slapdash work caused many mistakes.
examples.zh: 她草率的工作导致了许多错误。

definitions.en: n a coarse obnoxious person
definitions.zh: n. 懒散的人, 散漫的人

examples.en: The sloven never cleaned his room.
examples.zh: 那个懒散的人从不打扫房间。

examples.en: A sloven often leaves things in disorder.
examples.zh: 懒散的人常常把东西弄得乱七八糟。

definitions.en: v turn sharply; change direction abruptly
definitions.zh: v. (使)旋转

definitions.en: v move obliquely or sideways, usually in an uncontrolled manner
definitions.zh: n. 旋转

examples.en: The car began to slue on the ice.
examples.zh: 汽车在冰上开始打滑旋转。

examples.en: He slued the boat to avoid the rock.
examples.zh: 他猛地转船以避开岩石。

definitions.en: v. smear so as to make dirty or stained
definitions.zh: vt. 沾污, 弄脏
n. 脏污, 污点

examples.en: The mud smirched her white dress.
examples.zh: 泥巴弄脏了她的白裙子。

examples.en: A smirch on his reputation was hard to remove.
examples.zh: 他名誉上的污点很难去除。

definitions.en: n. powder (containing gypsum plaster and glue) that when mixed with water forms a plastic paste used to fill cracks and holes in plaster
definitions.zh: 一种抹墙粉的商标名；抹墙粉于...

examples.en: He used spackle to fill the hole in the wall.
examples.zh: 他用抹墙粉填补墙上的洞。

examples.en: Apply spackle to the crack before painting.
examples.zh: 在粉刷前把抹墙粉涂在裂缝上。

definitions.en: n a fact about some part (as opposed to general)
definitions.zh: n. 详情；细节；特性（specific的复数）

examples.en: Please give me the specifics of the plan.
examples.zh: 请给我这个计划的细节。

examples.en: We need specifics, not just general ideas.
examples.zh: 我们需要细节，而不仅仅是笼统的想法。

definitions.en: n. the scientific study of caves
definitions.zh: n. 洞穴学

examples.en: Speleology is the study of caves.
examples.zh: 洞穴学是研究洞穴的学科。

examples.en: He studied speleology to explore underground caves.
examples.zh: 他学习洞穴学以探索地下洞穴。

definitions.en: a. Not favored by the stars; ill-fated.
definitions.zh: a. 时运不济的, 运气不好的, 不幸的

examples.en: They were a star-crossed couple from the start.
examples.zh: 他们从一开始就是一对不幸的恋人。

examples.en: The star-crossed lovers could not be together.
examples.zh: 这对命运多舛的恋人无法在一起。

definitions.en: s used especially of persons
definitions.zh: a. 刚毅的, 大胆的

examples.en: The stouthearted soldier faced the enemy bravely.
examples.zh: 那位刚毅的士兵勇敢地面对敌人。

examples.en: She was stouthearted and never gave up.
examples.zh: 她刚毅不屈，从不放弃。

definitions.zh: a. 协作的, 协同的
[计] 协作的; 合作的

examples.en: The team worked in a synergic way.
examples.zh: 团队以协作的方式工作。

examples.en: Their synergic effort led to great success.
examples.zh: 他们的协同努力带来了巨大成功。

definitions.en: a. consisting of tendons or resembling a tendon
definitions.zh: a. 腱的
[医] 腱的, 腱性的

examples.en: The tendinous tissue connects muscle to bone.
examples.zh: 腱组织将肌肉连接到骨骼。

examples.en: He injured his tendinous fibers during the game.
examples.zh: 他在比赛中伤到了腱纤维。

definitions.en: s unwilling to part with money
definitions.zh: a. 吝啬的

examples.en: The tightfisted man never shared his money.
examples.zh: 那个吝啬的人从不分享他的钱。

examples.en: She is too tightfisted to buy a gift.
examples.zh: 她太吝啬了，不肯买礼物。

definitions.en: s repeated too often; overfamiliar through overuse
definitions.zh: a. 陈旧的, 老朽的

examples.en: The timeworn building needed repairs.
examples.zh: 那栋陈旧的建筑需要修缮。

examples.en: His timeworn jokes were no longer funny.
examples.zh: 他那些老掉牙的笑话不再好笑了。

definitions.en: v plate with tin
definitions.zh: a. 尖端的；有齿的

examples.en: The fork has four tined prongs.
examples.zh: 这把叉子有四个尖齿。

examples.en: A tined tool is useful for gardening.
examples.zh: 有齿的工具对园艺很有用。

definitions.en: a. of or relating to barbers and barbering
definitions.zh: a. 理发师的, 理发的

examples.en: He visited the tonsorial parlor for a haircut.
examples.zh: 他去理发店理发。

examples.en: Tonsorial services include shaving and styling.
examples.zh: 理发服务包括刮脸和造型。

definitions.en: s in utter disorder
definitions.zh: adv. 颠倒地, 乱七八糟地

definitions.en: r in a disordered manner
definitions.zh: a. 颠倒的, 乱七八糟的

definitions.en: r in disorderly haste
definitions.zh: n. 颠倒, 混乱

examples.en: The room was topsy-turvy after the party.
examples.zh: 派对后房间乱七八糟。

examples.en: His life turned topsy-turvy after the news.
examples.zh: 消息传来后，他的生活变得一团糟。

definitions.en: n. the trait of being easily persuaded
definitions.zh: n. 驯良, 温顺, 易处理

examples.en: The dog's tractability made training easy.
examples.zh: 这只狗的温顺使训练变得容易。

examples.en: Her tractability helped the team work smoothly.
examples.zh: 她的顺从帮助团队顺利工作。

definitions.en: n a hairdo formed by braiding or twisting the hair
definitions.zh: n. 女子的长发, 长而未束的女人头发

examples.en: She brushed her long tresses carefully.
examples.zh: 她仔细梳理她的长发。

examples.en: Her golden tresses shone in the sunlight.
examples.zh: 她的金色长发在阳光下闪闪发光。

definitions.en: n nonsensical talk or writing
definitions.zh: n. 华而不实的东西, 中看不中用的东西, 废物, 废话

definitions.en: n ornamental objects of no great value
definitions.zh: a. 虚有其表的, 浅薄的, 无用的

examples.en: The store sold cheap trumpery items.
examples.zh: 这家店出售廉价华而不实的东西。

examples.en: His speech was full of trumpery and nonsense.
examples.zh: 他的演讲充满了废话和空谈。

definitions.en: s. of sexual organs; stiff and rigid
definitions.zh: a. 肿胀的, 肿大的
[医] 肿胀的

examples.en: The tumid wound needed medical attention.
examples.zh: 肿胀的伤口需要医疗处理。

examples.en: His tumid ankle made walking difficult.
examples.zh: 他肿胀的脚踝使行走困难。

definitions.en: v. undergo ulceration
definitions.zh: vt. 使溃疡, 使腐败

definitions.en: v. affect with an ulcer
definitions.zh: vi. 溃烂, 腐败

examples.en: The wound began to ulcerate if not treated.
examples.zh: 伤口如果不处理会开始溃烂。

examples.en: Stress can cause the stomach lining to ulcerate.
examples.zh: 压力会导致胃黏膜溃疡。

definitions.en: a. Being beyond the world, or beyond the limits of our
definitions.zh: a. 世界之外的, 太阳系外的, 超俗的, 非现世的

examples.en: He studied ultramundane phenomena beyond Earth.
examples.zh: 他研究地球之外的超俗现象。

examples.en: The idea of ultramundane life fascinates many.
examples.zh: 超俗生命的想法让许多人着迷。

definitions.en: v. lend moral support to
definitions.zh: vt. 从底层加固, 支持, 加强

examples.en: Strong values undergird their friendship.
examples.zh: 坚定的价值观支撑着他们的友谊。

examples.en: Education should undergird a child's development.
examples.zh: 教育应该支持孩子的发展。

definitions.en: s not open to question; obviously true
definitions.zh: a. 无可置否的, 无疑问的

examples.en: The evidence is undisputable and clear.
examples.zh: 证据无可置疑且清晰。

examples.en: Her talent is an undisputable fact.
examples.zh: 她的才华是无可置疑的事实。

definitions.en: s. without envy or reluctance
definitions.zh: a. 不吝惜的, 慷慨的, 自愿的, 由衷的
[法] 出自内心的, 自愿的, 情愿的

examples.en: She gave ungrudging support to her friend.
examples.zh: 她慷慨地支持她的朋友。

examples.en: His ungrudging praise made everyone happy.
examples.zh: 他由衷的赞扬让每个人高兴。

definitions.en: n semisolid preparation (usually containing a medicine) applied externally as a remedy or for soothing an irritation
definitions.zh: n. 软膏, 药膏, 润滑油
[医] 软膏

examples.en: Apply this unguent to the dry skin.
examples.zh: 把这种软膏涂在干燥的皮肤上。

examples.en: The unguent soothed the burn quickly.
examples.zh: 药膏迅速缓解了烧伤。

definitions.en: s. free from emotional appeal; marked by reasonableness
definitions.zh: a. 没有热情的, 不动感情的

examples.en: He gave an unimpassioned speech about the facts.
examples.zh: 他就事实发表了冷静的演讲。

examples.en: Her unimpassioned response surprised everyone.
examples.zh: 她不动感情的回答让所有人惊讶。

definitions.en: n. the quality of unscrupulous dishonesty
definitions.zh: n. 狂妄；不择手段

examples.en: His unscrupulousness led to unethical decisions.
examples.zh: 他的不择手段导致了不道德的决定。

examples.en: The company's unscrupulousness harmed many people.
examples.zh: 这家公司的狂妄伤害了许多人。

definitions.en: s without soil or spot or stain
definitions.zh: a. 无斑点的, 无污点的, 无瑕疵的

examples.en: The white cloth remained unspotted after use.
examples.zh: 白布使用后依然无污点。

examples.en: Her reputation is unspotted and clean.
examples.zh: 她的名誉清白无瑕。

definitions.en: s not unfriendly or threatening
definitions.zh: 不威胁的

examples.en: The dog looked unthreatening and friendly.
examples.zh: 这只狗看起来不具威胁且友好。

examples.en: His unthreatening manner put everyone at ease.
examples.zh: 他不具威胁的态度让每个人放松。

definitions.en: a. of or relating to or similar to bears
definitions.zh: a. 熊的, 像熊的

examples.en: The ursine creature roamed the forest.
examples.zh: 那只像熊的动物在森林里游荡。

examples.en: He had an ursine appearance with a thick coat.
examples.zh: 他有着熊一般的外貌，毛发浓密。

definitions.en: s. foolishly fond of or submissive to your wife
definitions.zh: a. 溺爱妻子的, 一味顺从妻子的, 怕老婆的
[法] 对妻子过分宠爱的, 怕老婆的

examples.en: The uxorious husband always obeyed his wife.
examples.zh: 那个怕老婆的丈夫总是听从妻子。

examples.en: His uxorious behavior was often joked about.
examples.zh: 他溺爱妻子的行为常被开玩笑。

definitions.en: n. weak or sickly person especially one morbidly concerned with his or her health
definitions.zh: a. 有病的, 虚弱的, 过分担心健康的

definitions.en: a. of or relating to or characteristic of a person who is a valetudinarian
definitions.zh: n. 病弱的人, 过分担心健康的人

examples.en: The valetudinarian worried about every small ache.
examples.zh: 那个过分担心健康的人担心每一个小疼痛。

examples.en: He lived like a valetudinarian, always cautious.
examples.zh: 他像个病弱的人一样生活，总是小心翼翼。

definitions.en: v. change the appearance of, especially by marking with different colors
definitions.zh: vt. 使成斑驳, 使多样化

examples.en: The artist likes to variegate the colors.
examples.zh: 艺术家喜欢使颜色变得斑驳。

examples.en: Variegate the garden with different flowers.
examples.zh: 用不同的花使花园多样化。

definitions.en: v show off
definitions.zh: a. 自吹自擂的, 吹嘘的, 傲慢的

examples.en: His vaunting attitude annoyed his colleagues.
examples.zh: 他自吹自擂的态度惹恼了同事。

examples.en: She gave a vaunting speech about her success.
examples.zh: 她发表了一篇吹嘘自己成功的演讲。

definitions.en: s. habitually speaking the truth
definitions.zh: a. 说实话的, 诚实的, 老实的, 真实的

examples.en: A veracious person always tells the truth.
examples.zh: 诚实的人总是说实话。

examples.en: Her veracious account was trusted by everyone.
examples.zh: 她真实的叙述得到了每个人的信任。

definitions.en: s. appearing to be true or real
definitions.zh: a. 好像真实的
[法] 貌似真的, 似乎是真的, 很可能的

examples.en: The story seemed verisimilar and believable.
examples.zh: 这个故事看起来真实可信。

examples.en: A verisimilar explanation satisfied the audience.
examples.zh: 一个貌似真实的解释让观众满意。

definitions.en: n. A writer of verses; especially, a writer of
definitions.zh: n. 拙劣诗人

examples.en: The versemonger wrote poor poetry for money.
examples.zh: 那个拙劣诗人为了钱写差诗。

examples.en: No one took the versemonger seriously.
examples.zh: 没人把那个拙劣诗人当回事。

definitions.en: n. something that covers or cloaks like a garment
definitions.zh: n. 衣服, 衣裳, 覆盖物

definitions.en: v. provide or cover with a cloak
definitions.zh: vt. 给穿衣服

examples.en: The king wore a rich vesture of silk.
examples.zh: 国王穿着华丽的丝绸衣服。

examples.en: Snow vestured the ground in white.
examples.zh: 雪给大地披上了白衣。

definitions.en: n a stock or supply of foods
definitions.zh: n. 食物, 粮食

examples.en: The table was filled with delicious viands.
examples.zh: 桌子上摆满了美味的食物。

examples.en: They prepared viands for the long journey.
examples.zh: 他们为长途旅行准备了食物。

definitions.en: a. Full of, or subject to, changes.
definitions.zh: a. 世事变化的, 变迁的, 有盛衰的

examples.en: Life is vicissitudinous and full of changes.
examples.zh: 人生充满变迁，变化无常。

examples.en: Her vicissitudinous career had many ups and downs.
examples.zh: 她多变的职业生涯有许多起伏。

definitions.en: s having the sticky properties of an adhesive
definitions.zh: a. 粘的, 胶粘的, 粘质的
[医] 粘的

examples.en: The viscid glue stuck to my fingers.
examples.zh: 粘胶粘在了我的手指上。

examples.en: A viscid substance covered the table.
examples.zh: 一种粘性物质覆盖了桌子。

definitions.en: v. change into glass or a glass-like substance by applying heat
definitions.zh: vt.vi. (使)玻璃化

examples.en: Heat can vitrify sand into glass.
examples.zh: 热量可以将沙子玻璃化。

examples.en: The pottery will vitrify in the kiln.
examples.zh: 陶器在窑中会玻璃化。

definitions.en: v spread negative information about
definitions.zh: vt. 辱骂, 责骂
[法] 责骂, 辱骂, 谩骂

examples.en: He began to vituperate the driver loudly.
examples.zh: 他开始大声辱骂司机。

examples.en: Don't vituperate others when you are angry.
examples.zh: 生气时不要辱骂别人。

definitions.en: v compete for something; engage in a contest; measure oneself against others
definitions.zh: a. 竞争的
vie的现在分词

examples.en: The two teams are vying for the trophy.
examples.zh: 两支队伍正在争夺奖杯。

examples.en: Students are vying to win the scholarship.
examples.zh: 学生们正在竞争奖学金。

definitions.en: s. having tasteful clothing and being scrupulously neat
definitions.zh: a. 穿得考究的, 十分整洁的, 穿着考究的

examples.en: She always looks well-groomed and professional.
examples.zh: 她总是看起来整洁得体。

examples.en: A well-groomed man entered the room.
examples.zh: 一个穿着考究的男人走进了房间。

definitions.en: v overcome, as with emotions or perceptual stimuli
definitions.zh: vt. 用...覆盖, 压倒, 淹没
vi. 覆盖, 淹没

examples.en: Sadness began to whelm her heart.
examples.zh: 悲伤开始淹没她的心。

examples.en: The flood waters whelm the village.
examples.zh: 洪水淹没了村庄。

definitions.zh: n. 畏惧和憎恨外国人的人
[法] 仇视外国人, 恐惧外国人者, 害怕生人者

examples.en: A xenophobe dislikes people from other countries.
examples.zh: 仇外者不喜欢来自其他国家的人。

examples.en: He is a xenophobe who fears strangers.
examples.zh: 他是一个害怕陌生人的仇外者。

definitions.en: n plant adapted for life with a limited supply of water; compare hydrophyte and mesophyte
definitions.zh: n. 旱生植物

examples.en: A cactus is a typical xerophyte.
examples.zh: 仙人掌是一种典型的旱生植物。

examples.en: Xerophytes survive in dry deserts.
examples.zh: 旱生植物在干燥的沙漠中生存。
